intro: Near Milas, in Muğla province, lies Euromus, an ancient Carian city whose story runs from the 6th century BC to the 4th century AD. It is famous above all for one sight: its standing Temple of Zeus.
history: From the 6th century BC the city developed within the Carian world, and it passed through Persian and then Roman rule. Its great treasure is the Temple of Zeus Lepsinos, one of the best-preserved colonnaded temples in Anatolia.
structure-1: You are now before the Temple of Zeus Lepsinos, the temple of Zeus at Euromos. Look up: 16 of its columns are still standing, catching the light as they have for centuries.
highlights: As you wander, don't miss the stadium and the theatre, then the bouleuterion and the city walls.
facts: Did you know? An inscription on the temple records that it was dedicated in the name of Emperor Hadrian. With sixteen columns still standing, the Temple of Zeus Lepsinos is among the best-preserved temples in Anatolia. Look closely and you will see that some columns were never fluted: the temple was left unfinished, and the stone itself tells you so. Inscriptions on the columns even record, by name, which citizen paid for each one.
outro: This brings our journey through Euromus to an end. Please leave the stones untouched, keep to the marked paths and carry water with you. These columns have stood for centuries; let them keep standing for those who come after you. Enjoy your visit.
